# Adobe renewal and cancellation guide (as of 2026-11-17)

Adobe sells through several channels, and the rules differ by channel. Find out which one you're on first: individual or direct, Teams (direct or reseller), or VIP/VIP Marketplace (volume licensing).

## 1. Individual and direct plans (Creative Cloud, Acrobat)

**Default renewal behavior**
- Adobe says 
most Adobe plans renew automatically until you cancel
.
- Adobe's help page also says 
you currently can't stop a plan from renewing automatically. To turn off auto-renewal, you have to cancel the subscription.

- Exceptions Adobe lists: 
individual annual prepaid plans in Brazil and in Vermont can change auto-renewal settings in the Adobe account.

- Adobe's US subscription terms say that 
for automatic renewing customers in the United States, after the first year your subscription renews on a monthly basis until you cancel.
 Another regional version of the terms says 
for all other automatic renewing customers, the subscription renews annually after the first year
. The regional terms differ, so check your own region's page.
- One third-party site says 
US terms effective 1 August 2026 mean an annual plan billed monthly no longer rolls into a second full year by default.
 I couldn't confirm that effective date on Adobe's own pages. **Not verified — confirm in your signed contract or with the vendor.**
- Renewal price: 
prices may change, but only on renewal, and Adobe says it will inform you beforehand.


**Notice window**
- There's no fixed notice period in the sources I retrieved. The cost of cancelling depends on plan type and timing:
  - 
After 14 days, an annual plan paid monthly carries an early termination fee of 50% of the remaining contract balance.

  - 
For annual prepaid plans, a refund isn't possible if you cancel before the year ends.

  - A third-party guide says an annual plan 
can be cancelled in the last month of its term with no early termination fee
. This is not stated on the Adobe pages I retrieved, so treat it as **not verified** and check your own plan.
  - 
Cancelling within 14 days gives a full refund
, according to a third-party guide that matches Adobe's 14-day language.

**Steps to cancel (direct purchase)**
1. 
Sign in at account.adobe.com/plans, select Manage plan next to the subscription, then select Cancel your plan and follow the prompts.

2. 
Review the plan details, including any early termination fee, before continuing.

3. 
If you have more than one active Adobe plan, cancel each one separately.

4. After cancelling, 
the plan stays active until the end of the current billing period, and you keep access during that time.

5. If the online option is missing, a third-party source says 
Adobe's terms allow cancelling online or through Adobe Customer Support.
 I found no verified support email or notice address
